author: Shri Raghavendra Swami
commentary: प्राक् 'संन्यासस्त्वित्यादिना' संन्यासयोगौ मिलितावेव फलं साधयतः नान्यतर-परित्यागेनान्यतर इति नियमज्ञापनार्थं तयोः फलमुक्तं ब्रह्माधिगच्चति कुर्वन्न लिप्यत इत्यादिना ।  इदानीं तु तावेव मोक्षसाधनं न तु तदुभयत्यागेनान्यदिति नियमज्ञापनाय योगसंन्यासवतस्तदुभयाभाववतश्च मुक्तिसंसारविस्तारलक्षणं फलमाह ॥  युक्त इति ।  "कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वेत्यनेन" प्रागुक्तकामादिवर्जनरूपसंन्यासी ज्ञेयः ।  युक्तः भगवदर्पणबुद्ध्या कर्मानुष्ठानरूपयोगयुक्तः नैष्ठिकीं स्वाभाविकीं शान्तिं स्वरूपानन्दाविर्भावलक्षणां मुक्तिमाप्नोति ।  अयुक्तः योगहीनः कामकारेण फलकामादिना कर्मानुष्ठानेन संन्यासाभावेनेति यावत् ।  फले क्षुद्रफले सक्तो निबध्यते नितरां संसारमनुभवतीत्यर्थः ॥ ५.१२॥
translation:
He who abandoning the fruit of action follows Yoga obtains the natural peace. He who destitute of Yoga is by force of desire attached to the result is bound down.
V. Abandoning......action: of course, abandoning also desire, wish, thought, &c., of the fruit, i.e., becoming a Sanyasin as explained above. Follow's Yoga: performs duties regarding them acts of worship of the Lord, Natural: essential. Peace: the essential blessedness to which the soul is restored. He....desire: he who has not become a Sanyasin in the above sense, i.e., does not perform duties without motives or desires and simply for the Lord's grace. To the result: to the limited consequences of action, Is bound down: is subject to endless sufferings of birth and death
A. The Sanyasa has been (verse 8) explained as renouncing Abhimana with regard to the soul’s being an agent, by himself. Now the sense of the term is extended by stating that Sanyasa consists also in renouncing the Abhimana of thinking himself to be the director of another agent.
